cleanIntro: The Masai Mara is an INERTIA gun, and Retay says so in its own words: the shotgun runs on the kinetic energy of its own recoil, not on gas tapped from the barrel. ⚠ Retay publishes it as the Masai Mara LINE, in its own book with its own MM- part numbers. ⛔ Two sentences bracket this strip and neither is decoration: the bolt comes forward against a LOADED recoil spring and must be held while the carrier button is pressed, and on the way back together the recoil spring has to sit BETWEEN the locking head and the bolt or Retay warns a shot can be fired as the action closes.

steps.title: ⛔ Chamber, CARRIER and magazine — all three, before anything
steps.action: Retay's precondition for every operation on this shotgun names three places, not two: the chamber, the CARRIER, and the magazine. A shell sitting on the carrier is the one people miss, because it is not in the chamber and it is no longer in the tube.
steps.prose: Three places to look, and only one of them is obvious.
steps.quote: Before starting any operation on your shotgun, make sure that the chamber, carrier and the magazine are unloaded! (Carefully read the instructions on gun loading and unloading).
steps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Shotgun stripping (For cleaning and maintenance), p.72

steps.title: Open the bolt, then empty the TUBE through the carrier latch
steps.action: Open the bolt and let the chambered round extract and eject. Then reverse the gun, thrust the carrier inward and press the FRONT of the carrier latch with your index finger — one cartridge comes out per press. ⚠ The latch has to be pressed again for every shell; there is no single stroke that dumps the tube.
steps.prose: The magazine does not empty itself when the bolt opens. That is the step people skip.
steps.aside: 3) Reverse the gun and - thrusting the carrier towards inside - press the carrier latch frontal part with your index finger (fig. 28); the first cartridge will come out (fig. 29). The carrier latch must be pressed for each released cartridge.
steps.quote: 1) Open the bolt: the cartridge in the chamber will be extracted and ejected (fig. 25).
steps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Unloading, p.60

steps.title: Fore-end cap off, fore-end FORWARD off the magazine tube
steps.action: Unscrew the fore-end cap and slide the fore-end FORWARD along the magazine tube. ⚠ Read Retay's own parenthesis: this is the synthetic fore-end instruction. The book carves it out by name, so a wooden fore-end on the same gun is not covered by this step.
steps.prose: Forward, along the tube — not out sideways. The tube is the rail it rides.
steps.quote: 1) Unscrew the fore-end cap (figs. 3-4). Remove the fore-end making it slide, forward along the magazine tube (fig.5) (Only synthetic fore-end)
steps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Stripping procedure, step 1, p.74

steps.title: Open the bolt — and the cartridge drop lever if it will not stay
steps.action: Hold the gun in one hand and open the bolt with the other. If the bolt will not stay engaged to the rear, move the CARTRIDGE DROP LEVER as the arrow shows and repeat. That is Retay's own answer to a bolt that keeps running forward, and it is not a fault.
steps.prose: The drop lever is part of this strip, not just part of loading.
steps.quote: 2) Take the gun in one hand and with the other open the bolt (fig. 30); should the bolt fail to engage, move the cartridge drop lever as arrowed and repeat the operation (fig. 31).
steps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Stripping procedure, step 2, p.74

steps.title: Barrel, breech and fore-end come off the receiver as ONE assembly
steps.action: Rest the shotgun on your hip, hold it with one hand, and with the other pull the breech-barrel-fore-end assembly forward out of the receiver. It leaves as one unit; nothing here needs separating first.
steps.prose: Braced on the hip because it takes two hands and a straight pull, not because the gun is heavy.
steps.quote: 3) While resting the shotgun on your hip, keep it with one hand (fig. 32) and with the other hand pull the breech-barrel- fore-end assembly out of the receiver (fig. 33).
steps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Stripping procedure, step 3, p.74

steps.title: ⛔ HOLD THE BOLT — the recoil spring is loaded behind it
steps.action: Hold the bolt assembly with one hand to counter the thrust of the recoil spring, THEN press the carrier button and ease the bolt forward until the spring stops pushing it. ⛔ Pressing the button without holding the bolt lets a compressed spring drive it forward on its own.
steps.prose: This is the one moment in a Retay strip where energy is stored and a hand is the only thing holding it.
steps.caution: Glasses on, and ease it forward rather than letting it go.
steps.quote: 4) While holding the bolt assembly with one hand (fig. 34) so as to counter-balance the thrust of the recoil spring, push the carrier button and ease the bolt forward until the recoil spring no longer pushes it forward (fig. 35).
steps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Stripping procedure, step 4, p.76

steps.title: Bolt assembly out along its guides
steps.action: With the spring relaxed, pull the bolt assembly forward out of the receiver, sliding it along its guides. It runs on rails and comes out level; there is nothing here to lever.
steps.prose: If it binds it is not aligned. Straighten it rather than pulling harder.
steps.quote: 5) Pull the bolt assembly out of the receiver, sliding it along its guides (fig. 36).
steps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Stripping procedure, step 5, p.76

steps.title: ⚠ Firing pin retaining pin — hold the pin and its spring
steps.action: Take the firing pin retaining pin out of the bolt while HOLDING the firing pin and firing pin spring in place, then remove the pin and spring together. The retaining pin is the only thing containing that spring; let go first and both parts leave on their own.
steps.prose: The smallest spring in the gun and the easiest one to lose on a workshop floor.
steps.aside: 7) Remove the firing pin and firing pin spring from the bolt (fig. 38).
steps.quote: 6) Remove the firing pin retaining pin from the bolt assembly, while holding the firing pin and firing pin spring in place (fig. 37).
steps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Stripping procedure, step 6, p.76

steps.title: Locking head rotating pin, then the locking head
steps.action: Take the locking head ROTATING PIN out of its seat, then draw the bolt locking head out of the bolt. Order matters: the pin is what keys the head to the bolt, and the head will not come out until it is gone.
steps.prose: The rotating head is what locks this action shut. It is worth seeing clean.
steps.aside: 9) Remove the bolt locking head from the bolt (fig. 40).
steps.quote: 8) Remove the locking head rotating pin from its seat (fig. 39).
steps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Stripping procedure, step 8, p.78

steps.title: Recoil spring out of its seat — field strip complete
steps.action: Last, lift the recoil spring out of its seat in the bolt. That is Retay's published strip in full: fore-end, barrel group, bolt, firing pin and spring, locking head pin, locking head, recoil spring. ⛔ Anything past this is not in the book.
steps.prose: Ten numbered steps, and the maker stops there. So do we.
steps.quote: 10) Remove the recoil spring from its seat in the bolt (fig. 41).
steps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Stripping procedure, step 10, p.78

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Recoil spring BETWEEN the locking head and the bolt
deepSteps.action: On the way back together the recoil spring has one correct place, and Retay states the consequence of the wrong one: a shot fired during the closing phase. Check it is seated between the locking head and the bolt before the head goes in, not after.
deepSteps.prose: A reassembly note that names a discharge is not a fussy detail.
deepSteps.quote: NOTE: always make sure that the bolt recoil spring is positioned between the locking head and the bolt itself, in order to avoid a shot being fired during the closing phase.
deepSteps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Shotgun assembly, step 2, p.84
deepSteps.warn: WARNING: the slanted surfaces on the locking head’s stem should not be visible once the bolt locking head is mounted.

deepSteps.title: The locking head pin's reference line IS the assembly check
deepSteps.action: Retay gives you a way to see the locking head pin is right without taking anything apart again: the reference line on top of the pin must be VISIBLE and aligned with the bolt assembly's longitudinal axis.
deepSteps.prose: A visible witness mark is the maker telling you what correct looks like.
deepSteps.aside: 6) Insert the firing pin retaining pin in its seat, so as to block the firing pin (fig. 50).
deepSteps.quote: NOTE: the reference line on top of the pin must be visible and aligned with the bolt assembly longitudinal axis (fig. 48).
deepSteps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Shotgun assembly, step 4, p.84

deepSteps.title: ⚠ This gun runs on RECOIL, so the ammunition is a mechanical part
deepSteps.action: Retay names the mechanism plainly — the action is worked by the kinetic energy of recoil — and draws the consequence itself: the ammunition must be powerful enough to cycle the action. ⛔ On an inertia gun, light target loads a gas gun would digest can short-stroke.
deepSteps.prose: The cartridge is part of the operating system here, not just what comes out of the barrel.
deepSteps.aside: Use always ammunition that is powerful enough to fully cycle the action.
deepSteps.quote: Retay shotguns use the kinetic energy generated by the recoil to work the action.
deepSteps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Troubleshooting — Ammunition, p.64

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Never a case longer than the chamber
deepSteps.action: Retay's caution is unqualified and it states the stake: a case longer than the chamber has serious consequences for the shotgun AND the shooter. Check what the barrel is marked for before you check what the box says.
deepSteps.prose: The chamber length is stamped on the barrel for exactly this reason.
deepSteps.aside: Non-compliance to this rule would have serious consequences for both the shotgun and the shooter.
deepSteps.quote: CAUTION: never use cartridges with a case longer than the chamber.
deepSteps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Choice of ammunition, p.66

deepSteps.title: ⚠ The fore-end cap is a CHECK item, not just a fastener
deepSteps.action: Retay asks you to confirm the fore-end cap still carries its spring and, ESPECIALLY after the first rounds, that it is tightened firmly — its job is holding the barrel against the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: New gun, first outing, and the one fastener that walks loose.
deepSteps.quote: Check that the fore-end cap is fitted with spring and, especially after the first rounds, check that it is tightened firmly, to keep the barrel firmly against to the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Troubleshooting — Fore-end cap, p.64

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Choke tubes stay IN for cleaning
deepSteps.action: Retay forbids stripping the internal choke tubes out as part of cleaning and gives the reason: residue collects in the connection threads at the tube seat. ⚠ That is the opposite of the habit many owners bring from other guns.
deepSteps.prose: A prohibition with a mechanism attached is worth more than one without.
deepSteps.aside: Avoid that parts get in contact with oils containing solvents or chemical substances in general, which could alter or damage their surfaces.
deepSteps.quote: NOTE: whilst cleaning the gun the internal choke tubes are not to be stripped out. This in order to avoid residues collecting in the barrel’s internal choke tube’s connection threads.
deepSteps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Maintenance — cleaning note, p.70

deepSteps.title: Retay's own maintenance list — four controls, and no more
deepSteps.action: The book says the gun requires no special maintenance and then names the few controls it does want: the barrel cleaned after use, the firing mechanism cleared of powder residue, the bolt assembly periodically dismantled and lubricated, and corrosion-prone parts oiled.
deepSteps.prose: A short list from the maker beats a long one from anybody else.
deepSteps.aside: The following few controls are recommended: 1) Normal cleaning of the barrel after use;
deepSteps.quote: Thanks to its extreme simplicity and excellent materials, the Retay Automatic Shotgun requires no special maintenance.
deepSteps.cite: RETAY MASAI MARA LINE — USE • MAINTENANCE • SPARE PARTS — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Maintenance, p.68

cleaning.name: BARREL AND CHAMBER
tasks: Bore cleaned after use — Retay's first named control
⛔ Internal choke tubes LEFT IN — Retay forbids stripping them to clean
Chamber wiped dry; watch the threads at the choke tube seat

cleaning.name: BOLT AND FIRING MECHANISM
tasks: Bolt assembly dismantled, cleaned and lubricated periodically
Hammer and trigger cleared of powder residue
Locking head and its rotating pin checked before reassembly

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR AND STOCK
tasks: Parts exposed to weather lightly oiled against corrosion
⛔ No solvent-bearing oils on stock or fore-end surfaces
Fore-end cap spring present, and the cap re-tightened after the first rounds

reassembly: Recoil spring into its seat — ⛔ BETWEEN the locking head and the bolt, or Retay warns a shot can be fired as the action closes.
Locking head into the bolt, the hole on its stem lined up with the slot; the slanted surfaces on the stem must NOT be visible once it is home.
Locking head pin through the slot into the stem — reference line on top VISIBLE and aligned with the bolt's long axis.
Firing pin and its spring into the bolt hole, then the retaining pin in to block it.
Receiver held almost horizontal, bolt assembly into its guide.
Barrel-breech-fore-end assembly on, fore-end back along the tube, cap tightened firmly.
fncheck: With the gun confirmed unloaded, cycle the bolt by hand and confirm it locks and releases cleanly, then work the cartridge drop lever and the carrier latch and feel each one click. ⛔ Then check the fore-end cap again — Retay singles it out as the thing to re-tighten after the first rounds, because a loose cap lets the barrel shift against the receiver. Confirm the locking-head pin's reference line is visible and square to the bolt before the gun goes back in the cabinet.
